position: Reform the Negotiated Rulemaking Process at ED
proposal: The Mandate recommends that the Department work with Congress to amend the Higher Education Act to eliminate the negotiated rulemaking requirement for Title IV and related regulations, or at a minimum allow the Department to use public hearings in place of negotiated rulemaking sessions. It criticizes the process as expensive and slow, with a master calendar that complicates timely rule updates.

status_summary: No law or bill amending Section 492 of the Higher Education Act to remove or replace negotiated rulemaking was found as of 2026-10-12. The Department has continued to use the process: it held a public hearing on 2025-08-07 and convened the RISE (student loans) committee in fall 2025, the AHEAD (Workforce Pell and accountability) committee in December 2025 and January 2026, and the AIM (accreditation) committee in April and May 2026, with proposed rules published 2026-01-30, 2026-03-09 and 2026-08-20. ED's RISE proposed rule states that it complies with Section 492 and that the 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21) does not waive negotiated rulemaking, while arguing that the law implicitly waived the master calendar for provisions effective 2026-07-01.

timeline.event: ED published a notice of a public hearing on 2025-08-07 and its intent to establish negotiated rulemaking committees to implement the 2025 reconciliation law's higher education provisions, citing HEA section 492.
The RISE negotiated rulemaking committee concluded its second session; a second committee (AHEAD) met in December 2025 and January 2026.

ED published the RISE proposed rule, stating that the committee reached consensus on 2025-11-06, that the rule complies with HEA section 492, and that P.L. 119-21 does not waive negotiated rulemaking; the AHEAD proposed rule followed on 2026-03-09 per the ED program page.
ED published a proposed rule on accreditation recognition reflecting consensus reached by the AIM negotiated rulemaking committee, which met in April and May 2026.
